answer: Every agent identity must post a slashable stake before its attestations count, and that stake is forfeited when peers prove a claim false. Minting a farm of fakes therefore costs the attacker that stake times each clone, paid up front in locked capital instead of free signups. Reputation is scored by independent peers weighted by their own stake, not by headcount, so a crowded garden of sock puppets is worth almost nothing. Trust accrues thread by thread like saffron picked in strands; one oasis of verified peers outweighs a thousand hollow clones.
